match.reason: The new point covers the Revolution as a whole, including the overthrow of the king and the spread of its ideas, while the bank card covers only the 1789 Declaration of the Rights of Man and is written at a more advanced depth than Stage 5.

draft.title: The French Revolution
card: In 1789 many people in France were angry. Most paid heavy taxes and had little say in how the country was run, while the king ruled with great power.
From 1789 the French overthrew their king. In 1792 France became a republic, a country with no king, and King Louis XVI was executed in 1793.
In 1789 the revolutionaries issued the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen. It said people are born free and equal in rights, and that laws should apply to everyone.
These ideas spread beyond France: equality (people have the same rights), democracy (people have a say in government) and the rule of law (everyone, even rulers, must obey the law).
draft.remember: The French overthrew their king and declared rights for all citizens, spreading equality, democracy and the rule of law.

a.q: Which idea did the French Revolution spread, as set out in the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen?
opts: Everyone, even rulers, must obey the law
Kings rule because God chose them
Only land owners should have rights
Rulers may change laws to suit themselves
a.why: The Declaration said laws should apply to everyone, which is the rule of law. The other options defend the power of rulers or limit rights, which is what the revolutionaries were opposing.
a.clue: The revolutionaries were against unlimited power for the king.

b.q: In 1830, a group in another country demands that all men have a vote and that their king must obey the same laws as everyone else. Which French Revolution ideas are they using?
opts: Democracy and the rule of law
Industry and the rule of law
Equality and rule by one family
b.why: Having a vote is democracy, because people have a say in government. A king who must obey the same laws is the rule of law. The options with a strong monarchy or rule by one family go against what the group is demanding.
b.clue: Match each demand to an idea: a vote, and a king under the law.

a.best: Everyone, even rulers, must obey the law

b.best: Democracy and the rule of law

check.summary: No problems found. The dates (1789 revolution, 1792 republic, 1793 execution of Louis XVI) and the Declaration's content are correct, and both questions have one clearly right answer that matches the card.
